figures.caption: Fig. 3: Overview of BlazeVGGT. At each global-attention block, camera tokens from all input frames define a view-level similarity structure, from which greedy DPP [2] selection retains a diverse subset of frames. All frames remain in the Query path, while the selected frame blocks provide the Key–Value context for global attention; the resulting features are passed to the camera and depth heads.
figures.visual_observation: Main agent viewed original pixels: image is a method pipeline with named stages/attention paths, not a result visualization.

figures.caption: Figure 2: Overview of HiP3R. Frozen backends predict overlapping chunks. Stage I builds a chunk-level Sim⁡(3)\mathrm{Sim}(3) graph from overlap and loop constraints to recover layout and scale. Stage II estimates one shared SE⁡(3)\mathrm{SE}(3) camera per frame under that layout.
figures.visual_observation: Main agent viewed original pixels: image is a method pipeline with named stages/attention paths, not a result visualization.

figures.caption: Fig. 2: The proposed system is integrated into ORB-SLAM3. A panoptic perception module periodically discovers semantically known and unknown movable objects (blue block) in the scene, while a lightweight propagation module updates object masks between panoptic inferences. Object identities and motion estimates are maintained in a persistent object list (yellow block). Dynamic object masks are then used to remove dynamic ORB features from the localization and mapping framework.
figures.visual_observation: Main agent re-viewed original pixels: pipeline/architecture with named stages, not result image.

figures.caption: Figure 4. Streaming dynamic segmentation architecture. Left: standard causal streaming reconstruction with a KV Cache, where each frame attends only to past tokens. Right: our Stream4D augments the causal pipeline with motion-decoupled masking. Queries load cached keys/values to compute attention scores, aggregate temporal saliency across frames, and produce dynamic masks. These masks are then applied to modify the cached keys, effectively suppressing interference from dynamic regions during historical aggregation.
figures.visual_observation: Main agent re-viewed original pixels: pipeline/architecture with named stages, not result image.

figures.caption: Figure 1: AOV-GS system overview. Online loop: posed RGB-D updates a Gaussian map; the planner selects NBVs; CLIP mask embeddings are extracted in parallel on keyframes. Offline stage: a language field is trained on Gaussians and queried by text.
figures.visual_observation: Main agent re-viewed original pixels: pipeline/architecture with named stages, not result image.

figures.caption: Fig. 2: Overview of the proposed framework. Frozen VGGT-Omega features from an RGB window are adapted into feature pyramids and frame memories. Historical residual proposals refine a latest-frame BEV anchor through cellwise selective fusion with a learned no-update option. Observation-aware evidential heads produce occupancy, spatial support, and confidence. Right: predicted occupancy with paths to example goals, planned path projections into the latest RGB view, and uncertainty 1−cj1-c_{j}.
figures.visual_observation: Main agent re-viewed original pixels: pipeline/architecture with named stages, not result image.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Overview of RecallGS. Given a posed observation and the observation history, RecallGS recalls candidate views via CLIP, verifies their geometric support with rendering responsibility, and replays the verified features to build an online 3DGS reconstruction with a semantic field
